# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser-native top-down arcade driving sandbox called Vice Grid: Wanted Run. Preserve the source mechanics: four touch/keyboard vehicle controls, acceleration/friction steering, procedural city grid with blocking buildings, cash pickups worth $500, pedestrian collisions worth $50 and one wanted star up to five, police pursuit only when wanted heat exists, collision damage, health-based failure, and restart. Transform presentation into a satirical GTA-inspired open-city chase with dirty cash HUD, wheel health, wanted stars, neon civic blocks, glowing stolen car focal identity, police cruiser visuals, compact mobile controls, and darkly comic Busted failure copy.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: top-down open-city arcade driving sandbox.
- objective: drive through a procedural city grid, collect glowing cash drops, survive collisions, and create optional chaos.
- input model: keyboard arrows plus four large touch buttons for left, right, gas, and brake.
- core loop: start run, spawn city/player/loot, steer vehicle, collect loot for +500, collide with pedestrians for +50 and wanted escalation, avoid walls/traffic/police damage, continue until health reaches zero.
- fail/friction state: wall and vehicle impacts damage health; zero health shows the busted/game-over restart screen.

## Protected mechanics
- Four-button vehicle input, acceleration, reverse braking, turn direction tied to travel direction, friction, speed clamps.
- Procedural 30x30 tile city with roads, buildings as blocking walls, and parks/passable open spaces.
- Loot spawns on non-building tiles and awards exactly $500 on contact.
- Pedestrian contact at speed awards exactly $50 and increases wanted heat by one up to five.
- Traffic spawns around the player; police vehicles pursue only when wanted heat is active.
- Wall and traffic collisions damage player health by 5 and game over occurs at zero health.

## Remixed target
Vice Grid: Wanted Run reframes the preserved driving sandbox as a satirical mobile-first open-city crime-chaos chase. The player is a stolen neon street machine making bad decisions for dirty cash while wanted stars, police cruisers, collision flashes, and civic-themed game-over copy express the GTA-inspired prompt without changing scoring, controls, collisions, or fail semantics.
